blocks.p: Two matrices can be added only if they have the same order; add entry by entry. Multiplying by a scalar multiplies every entry:

blocks.math: \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} e & f \\ g & h \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} a+e & b+f \\ c+g & d+h \end{bmatrix}, \qquad k\begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} ka & kb \\ kc & kd \end{bmatrix}

blocks.p: $AB$ is defined when the number of columns of $A$ equals the number of rows of $B$. An $m \times n$ matrix times an $n \times p$ matrix gives an $m \times p$ matrix, and each entry is the sum of products of a row of $A$ with a column of $B$.
Calculate $AB$ and $AC$. ($B$ is 3×3 and $C$ is 3×1, so $B + C$ isn't defined.)
For example, the top-left entry is row 1 of $A$ times column 1 of $B$: $(1)(2) + (-2)(-1) + (3)(1) = 7$.

sections.heading: Worked example: AB and BA differ

blocks.p: So $PQ \ne QP$: matrix multiplication isn't commutative. Also, a product can be zero without either factor being zero: $Z = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ is not the zero matrix, but $Z^2 = O$.

list: $A(BC) = (AB)C$ and $A(B + C) = AB + AC$, whenever the products are defined.
$(AB)^T = B^TA^T$, with the order reversed. For $A$ and $B$ above, this holds entry by entry.
$AI = IA = A$ for the identity matrix of matching order.
**Assuming $AB = BA$.** It usually doesn't, as $PQ$ and $QP$ show.
**Multiplying entry by entry.** That's not matrix multiplication; use rows times columns.
**Cancelling a matrix.** $AB = AC$ doesn't imply $B = C$ unless $A$ is invertible.

exam.note: The 2025-26 CBSE Class XII syllabus lists operations on matrices (addition, multiplication and multiplication by a scalar), the non-commutativity of multiplication and non-zero matrices whose product is the zero matrix. JEE Main 2026 lists the algebra of matrices, and JEE Advanced 2026 lists addition, multiplication by a scalar and product of matrices, and the transpose.

related.intro: Recognising special matrix shapes and their properties builds directly on these operations.
